explanation: Many larger Philippine restaurants already add a mandatory service charge (commonly 10%) under Republic Act 11360 (2019), which effectively functions as the tip, so no extra payment is expected on top of it. If no service charge appears on the bill, leaving about 10% in cash is a welcome but optional gesture of appreciation.
local_tip: Check the bill for an existing 'service charge' line before tipping extra; if there isn't one, leave roughly 10% in cash directly with the server.
regional_note: In tourist hubs like Boracay or Cebu, extra tipping on top of the service charge is more common than in small provincial eateries, where it is rare and sometimes refused.

also_check.note: Tipping is considered unnecessary and can embarrass staff, who may refuse the money since service is already included.
Tipping 15-20% is standard and expected for sit-down restaurant service.
Service charge is included by law, but leaving small change for good service is a nice gesture.

sources.title: How much do Pinoys tip in restaurants?
